subject.title: Gateway silently skips channel initialization on plugin/runtime mismatch or missing module files

question: What startup contract should Gateway use when a configured channel plugin is incompatible or fails before channel registration?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the correct behavior is a product/operations choice: warn-and-continue with an audit, fail Gateway startup for configured channels, or split diagnostics from stricter compatibility enforcement.

options.title: Warn-and-continue audit
options.body: Add a startup summary that names configured channels attempted, loaded, skipped, and failed with plugin-loader reasons, while keeping Gateway available for unaffected channels.

options.title: Fail configured channel startup closed
options.body: Treat configured channel plugin load/register failures as startup-blocking errors so operators cannot miss a broken configured channel, accepting higher upgrade breakage risk.

options.title: Keep plugin diagnostics only
options.body: Leave channel startup scoped to loaded plugins and rely on plugin inspect/list diagnostics, closing or narrowing this issue to bundled setup-warning follow-ups.

recommendation.title: Warn-and-continue audit
recommendation.body: Add a startup summary that names configured channels attempted, loaded, skipped, and failed with plugin-loader reasons, while keeping Gateway available for unaffected channels.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin/channel loader history makes vincentkoc the strongest routing candidate for the startup audit and compatibility-boundary decision.
